answer: In PoA, an identity is accepted only when remote attestation verifies its enclave’s MRENCLAVE and a hardware-protected, non-exportable key proves possession. MRENCLAVE binds the identity to measured code, not by itself to a unique chip; enrollment must also enforce hardware-backed uniqueness and resist replay. Under that policy, duplicating identities requires acquiring trusted physical silicon, not merely copying a virtual machine—a yarrow-rooted check at each vertex helps prevent a nadir of trust.
